content.text: Now I'll add a booking test that checks the 201 and the 500 body.

Booking works again. `createAppointment` inserted into a column called `created_by`, but the schema's column is `created_by_user_id`, so every insert failed. I fixed that in `src/repos/appointments.ts`.

`route()` in `src/lib/http.ts` now handles unexpected errors differently. It logs one error line with an `errorId`, the route (method and path only) and a sanitized cause, and returns `{ "errorId": "err_…" }` with the 500. The cause keeps only the error name, code, errno and sqlState. The message is included only for non-database errors and a few schema-only database codes, because mysql2 errors carry the full SQL text and can quote row values such as the visit reason. Requests carry no patient data in URLs or query strings, so the Apache access log has nothing to leak.

I added a POST booking test that expects a 201 with an `apt_` id, and `npm run verify` passes (19 tests). I did not add a test for the new 500 response, so the `errorId` body and log line haven't been exercised by a test.
